title: Log back in to a bank portal that the browser already knows
description: On the logged-out page or the login page of an Atruvia / VR banking portal: leaves the logged-out page for the login page, then presses Anmelden and waits for the start page with its Postfach button. It never types a PIN or password: the browser's own password manager has to have filled the VR-NetKey and the PIN. If the portal asks for a second factor, the run ends with needs_person: a TAN field (kind code, pass the relayed TAN as param code and resume at the step in next), or an approval on the person's own device such as SecureGo or a new-device check (kind device). If the login page stays (no saved PIN), it ends with needs_person kind login. Matched on any bank's domain by the portal's paths.

params.name: code
params.description: The one-time code (TAN) the person relayed after a needs_person of kind code. Never invent one.

steps.note: Only the logged-out page has this button; on the login page the step is skipped.

steps.failMessage: The login page did not appear. Ask the person to open the bank portal and log in themselves.

steps.note: Presses the button only. The browser's password manager must already have filled the fields.
Lets the page after the button settle before the second-factor checks look at it.
Success is checked first: a page with the Postfach button is logged in, whatever promo headings it carries (the portal advertises "Browsererkennung" on its own pages).

steps.prompt: Approve the login on your own device (SecureGo or a new-device check), then tell me.
The bank asks for a TAN. Please give me the current code.

steps.note: Skipped unless the run resumed with a code.
Only after a code was typed; the button names are not verified against a live page.

steps.prompt: The login page is still open: no PIN was saved. Please log in yourself, then tell me.

steps.failMessage: Not logged in: the start page did not appear. Beifahrer never fills a PIN or a password. Ask the person to log in themselves, then continue.
